projects.title: RELICFALL · Beneath the Beacon
projects.description: Top-down lighthouse-keeper roguelike descending from normal maintenance cellars into randomized hellish strata. Mobile auto-fire settings, dodge, and agent-forged weapons.
projects.genre: Top-down action roguelike / nautical psychological horror

nodes.title: Game Design Bible
nodes.content:
# Game Design Bible

## High concept
*Relicfall: Beneath the Beacon* combines **Brotato's immediate combat**, **Hades-style meaningful upgrades**, and escalating psychological horror. You are the keeper of the last functioning lighthouse. Its beam once sealed something underneath the coast.

## Player fantasy
A solitary, ordinary lighthouse keeper survives hell not with heroic animations but through movement, resolve, an oil lantern and a fantastical weapon forged by the building agent.

## Player-facing loop
**5 seconds:** position, target, fire, read enemy telegraphs, dodge.
**45 seconds:** clear an uncanny chamber, collect embers and an upgrade.
**3 minutes:** descend a floor, see recognizable fixtures degrade, beat an elite.
**15–25 minutes:** pass eight increasingly twisted strata and confront the buried light source. For prototype a 6–10 minute partial route is appropriate.

## Run structure
- One lighthouse surface intro; descend into floors 1–8.
- Each floor consists of 2–4 generated chambers, with an elite/boss chamber at selected intervals.
- Rooms are hand-designed modular layouts combined using seeded RNG, with enemy packs, props, encounter modifiers and rewards rolled independently.
- Room completion unlocks a downward hatch or door; camera cuts to the next room rather than scrolling the whole world.
- Permanent unlocks are optional future work; death restarts from above the cellar.

## Boundaries
- No pay-to-win, cryptocurrency, real-world loot boxes, or avatar animation dependency.
- Must work on Android touch and desktop keyboard/mouse.
- Keep fair hit indicators, hit pause, readable 2D contrast and stable 60 fps target (30 fps minimum on weak phones).

## Prototype-first scope
1 character, 1 agent-created starter weapon, 4 enemies, 8 themes, seeded rooms, auto-fire setting, dodge, one boss, XP/upgrades, death/retry.

nodes.title: Keeper Character & Story Beats
nodes.content:
# The Lighthouse Keeper

## Design
- **Identity:** The Last Keeper (renameable later), isolated but practical, long dark coat, oilskin hood, heavy sea boots, brass keys, extinguished lantern.
- **Static avatar:** baseline idle still works as the whole game avatar. Move by sliding a single frame; face through mirror/rotation or directional sprites only if provided.
- **Silhouette:** small hood, rounded lantern glow, angular coat taper, white/amber light that always contrasts with floor.
- **Emotions without animating:** a halo dimming on hurt; lantern brightening on heal; trail/dust on dodge; coat colour changes when cursed.

## Story through environment
- The stairwell seems to lead under the building; measurements stop agreeing.
- The keeper finds maintenance notes in their own handwriting dated centuries earlier.
- At deeper levels the lighthouse beam shines *up* through cracks from below.
- The final chamber reveals a sun imprisoned as the lamp's original fuel.

## Narrative pickups (example)
1. `Pump Maintenance — Salt Pump 2`: ordinary work order.
2. `Waterline Log`: water has risen against gravity.
3. `Keeper Register`: the keeper signed it every year for 400 years.
4. `The Mirror Crew`: reports of workers with lamps instead of faces.
5. `Final order`: extinguish the false sun, or feed it your own light.

## Endings (later)
- **Keep the Light:** become new immortal keeper.
- **Break the Lens:** release the light at a terrible cost.
- **Walk Away:** only possible after discovering all sealed notes.

nodes.title: START HERE
nodes.content:
# RELICFALL — Beneath the Beacon

**Genre:** top-down 2D action roguelike | **Lead:** The Last Lighthouse Keeper | **Target:** Project0 mobile & desktop | **Status:** Design + standalone prototype.

## Premise
A remote lighthouse goes dark during a storm. The keeper climbs down to the perfectly ordinary maintenance cellar to restore power. Every floor below becomes less possible: saltwater seeps upward, rooms shift, history rots, and hell opens under the light. The only way back is to drag the lighthouse's stolen flame to the heart of the abyss.

## Player character
The **Lighthouse Keeper**: weatherworn coat, yellow oilskin hood, brass keys, lantern; usually a static 2D avatar/sprite, even while moving. Attacks, dodges, weapons, lantern light and enemies animate independently. An existing custom avatar may be used if host APIs support it; do not assume automatic access to Project0 identity or avatar model.

## Three game pillars
1. **A lighthouse becoming hell:** every descent retains normal-world features twisted progressively into infernal nightmares.
2. **The agent forges your first weapon:** the builder designs an original signature weapon with working attacks, art, JSON stats, animation sheet and lore (not just a description).
3. **Good on a phone:** automatic fire enabled by default on mobile, reversible in Settings, plus an intentional dodge button and clear telegraphs.

## Start here in Workshop
1. Read **Combat & Mobile Settings** and **Dodge & Invulnerability**.
2. Read **Agent Weapon Forge Brief** and give the agent the build instructions from **Agent Master Prompt**.
3. Check **Sprite Atlas Standard** and open the attached layout PNGs in Assets. Every animation must follow this layout and JSON metadata.
4. Open the stand-alone `prototype/index.html` to test movement, auto-fire, dodge and room descent.
5. Add artwork to Assets and refine mechanic notes. This Workshop import is editable; it does not publish a Project0 experience.

## Release guardrails
- Confirm current Project0 game docs and integration restrictions before implementation in an actual lot.
- Keep user API keys and account credentials out of builds and notes.
- Do not publish a public lot without the owner's explicit approval.
- Multiplayer and real-time AI artwork generation are **not** assumed supported or in scope.

nodes.title: Combat Balance & XP
nodes.content:
# Combat Balance and Levelling

## Baseline keeper
- HP: 100; walk speed: 190 px/s; hurt i-frame: 0.45 s.
- Dodge: 120 px / 0.22 sec, 0.16-s i-frame, 1.5-s cooldown.
- Healing drops restore 12–22 HP; no automatic regeneration except rare shrine.
- Auto Fire: ON for Android; per-device preference persisted.

## XP
- Required XP: `20 + 10 * (level-1)` for levels 1–5, then increase modestly.
- Three cards at each level-up, reroll only when an upgrade provides it.
- Pauses action while cards are displayed.

## Suggested upgrade cards
| Perk | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Steady Hands | -9% weapon cooldown (floor 0.3s) |
| Wicked Wick | +15% weapon damage |
| Polished Lens | +15% reach |
| Sea Boots | +12% move speed |
| Hot Brass | +12% area / splash radius |
| Second Chance | +1 extra dodge charge (rare) |
| Keeper's Breath | +20 max HP and heal 20 |
| Lamp Fuel | Next 6 kills drop extra embers |
| Evasive Memory | -12% dodge cooldown |
| Black Salt | Hit enemies apply 1.5-sec slow |

## Enemy progression guardrail
Scale **one lever at a time** per floor: enemy HP, encounter count, attack frequency, or room hazard density. Do not multiply all four steeply together. A beginner should reach floors 2–3 in their first few tries, not die in the first ten seconds.

nodes.title: Dodge & Invulnerability
nodes.content:
# Dodge Mechanics

**Core idea:** a desperate sidestep/lunge: no animated avatar is required. The player slides rapidly in the chosen direction with spectral afterimages and a bright lantern flash.

## First balancing target
| Setting | Target |
| --- | --- |
| Dodge distance | 120 world px |
| Dodge duration | 0.22 seconds |
| Invulnerable window | 0.16 seconds from dodge start |
| Cooldown | 1.5 seconds after activation |
| Direction | joystick or movement keys, else last facing direction |
| Collision | slide against walls; NEVER pass through solid props or doors |
| Charges | 1 initially; upgrade can add one later |
| On use | brief amber afterimage + high-contrast ring |

## Input priority
- Dodge must work while auto-fire is active.
- Ignore dodge input during pause or death.
- If pressed during manual fire, dodge can cancel the weapon's recovery but cannot cancel an already-fired projectile.
- While dodging, disable hostile contact damage *only* during actual i-frames; environmental pits may still be hazardous if explicitly signaled.

## Readable telegraphs
- Enemy windups ≥ 0.45 s for dangerous attacks on mobile.
- Every boss attack should have a consistent floor warning AND audio/shape cue.
- Give player ~0.3 s after a room transition before aggression begins.

## Acceptance
1. Dodge through one enemy strike without taking damage if inside 0.16-s iframe.
2. Damage after the i-frame expires works normally.
3. Dodge stops at walls and doesn't teleport through obstacles.
4. Holding DODGE does not automatically consume the next recharge.
5. Cooldown bar drains or fills clearly on phone.

nodes.title: Mobile Settings & Auto Fire
nodes.content:
# Mobile Settings — auto-fire is ON by default

## Critical requirement
Mobile launches with **Auto Fire = ON** on a fresh install. Settings has a plainly labeled **Auto Fire ON/OFF toggle**, available from pause and main menu, and remembers the choice across runs (`localStorage` or supported host save API).

## When Auto Fire is ON
- Aim at closest eligible enemy **in range and visible**; prefer the enemy closest to the facing/aim direction when manual aim is active.
- Fire on weapon cooldown, even while moving or dodging (subject to weapon's explicit cancel rules).
- Respect collision/line of sight. Never auto-target through a sealed wall.
- If no valid enemy exists, don't waste shots (unless weapon is explicitly an always-firing pattern).
- Visual targeting ring allows the player to know which enemy will be hit.

## When Auto Fire is OFF
- Show large right-side **FIRE** touch button (hold to repeat according to cooldown).
- On desktop: mouse hold / Space to shoot, with optional auto-fire toggle.
- Aiming: prefer last touch direction or nearest enemy, then manual right-stick drag in later versions.
- Switching back ON immediately resumes targeting.

## Controls
| Input | Desktop | Phone/tablet |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Move | WASD / arrows | Large floating joystick, bottom-left |
| Fire | Mouse hold / Space (when manual) | Fire button (when manual) |
| Dodge | Shift / right click | Large DODGE button, bottom-right |
| Pause / Settings | P or gear | Gear button, top-right |
| Upgrade choice | Keys 1-3 or click | Tap large cards |
| Interact | E | Interact button if needed |

## Settings scope
- Auto Fire (on by default for mobile; configurable desktop)
- Aim Assist (on/off; independent of Auto Fire)
- Screen Shake (on/off)
- Reduced Motion (on/off)
- Damage Numbers (on/off)
- Sound/Music volume (future)
- Contrast Mode (future)

## UX acceptance tests
- Fresh Android starts firing automatically when monsters appear.
- OFF genuinely stops fire until manual input; FIRE button becomes visible.
- Settings persist after reload; toggling does not reset the run.
- Touch joystick and dodge work concurrently (multi-touch).
- Buttons are at least 48 CSS px; respect safe-area insets and screen orientation changes.
- No background firing while paused, selecting a level-up or game over.

nodes.title: Agent Asset Request Template
nodes.content:
# New Agent-Made Weapon — Reusable Request

Copy and customize this into any agent task:

> Invent, draw and integrate ONE new weapon into RELICFALL: Beneath the Beacon. It must visually fit the Lighthouse Keeper and the current depth. Deliver: (a) a filled stats JSON validated against `weapon.schema.json`; (b) transparent weapon idle/swing sprite sheet following atlas standard; (c) projectile / impact / special effects sheets as needed; (d) one 64px inventory icon; (e) engine implementation with collisions and no wall penetration; (f) tested mobile auto/manual fire; (g) balance explanation and an exact list of generated files. Prefer original game mechanics, not reused generic swords. Do not overwrite existing working weapons or publish publicly without approval.

## Weapon review worksheet
**Proposed name:**
**Archetype and origin story:**
**Sprite readability at 32px:**
**Damage / cadence / range:**
**Unique ability:**
**Combo upgrades:**
**Tests passed:**
**Files to attach:**
**Status:** Idea / Needs art / Needs testing / Accepted

nodes.title: Agent Weapon Forge Brief
nodes.content:
# Agent Weapon Forge — mandatory first step

The **building agent** must create an original starter weapon that belongs to the Lighthouse Keeper. Do not use a generic stock sword. The weapon must exist as a real asset with collision mechanics, a data file and an animation atlas or documented procedural animations.

## Creative source material
Design around nautical relics, brass lighthouse machinery, lenses, oil, shipwreck tools, salt, signal lamps, bells, anchor hooks, or condemned sea life. The deeper world contains infernal variants; the starting weapon should still resemble a **believable keeper tool made supernatural**.

## Required output from the agent
1. Original weapon name, silhouette, clear lore in ≤ 3 sentences.
2. Choose one **archetype** (lantern-focus, flare-gun, harpoon, chain-hook, signal-bell, salt-sprayer, arc-lens, crank-blade) and one attack behaviour (bolt, arc, beam, melee sweep, thrown return, orbiting, burst).
3. One **distinct special mechanic** beyond +damage: ricochet off wet walls, flare marks, oil pool ignition, timed recall, charged bell shockwave, heat buildup, target tether, etc.
4. Fair stats compatible with the balance table. No instant-kill or firing through walls.
5. Draw/source **actual weapon art** (PNG, SVG or code-rendered vector), a thumbnail, 8-frame 64px layout as appropriate, muzzle flash/impact VFX, and data JSON. If no raster generator exists, use handcrafted SVG and save it.
6. Implement actual target selection, projectile / hit detection, firing cadence and FX in game.
7. Run mobile tests with Auto Fire ON and OFF and report exact results.

## Example *only* — agent should improve or replace
**The Wickpiercer** (first agent-made version): a brass harpoon launcher built from the lamp's pressure regulator. Fires amber lance bolts. Every fifth enemy hit leaves a suspended flare that detonates after 0.8 s. Baseline: 13 damage, 0.72-s cooldown, 245px range, 440px/s projectile, 8px collision radius. Actual 64px weapon atlases, icon and directionless effect sheets are bundled in the asset library.

## Creative pass/fail rubric (out of 10 each)
- Fits keeper/lighthouse fiction
- Distinct silhouette at 32px
- Readable on a dark background
- A special ability with interesting player decisions
- Balanced sustained DPS / attack windows
- Usable without avatar animation
- Clear mobile target effects
- All visual files actually exist
- JSON fields match real gameplay
- Audio + accessibility alternatives

**Accept only ≥ 80/100 with no zero in gameplay functionality or asset existence.**

nodes.title: Weapon Data Schema & Example
nodes.content:
# Weapon JSON Contract

**Source of truth:** `weapons/starter-weapon.json` and `weapons/weapon.schema.json` in export package. Stats are editable; game loads a validated data object rather than relying on prose.

## Must-have fields
- `id`, `name`, `lore`, `archetype`, `element`, `rarity`, `damage`, `cooldownSeconds`, `rangePx`, `projectileSpeedPxPerSec`, `collisionRadiusPx`, `aimMode`, `shotCount`, `special`, `asset`, `animation`, `audio`.
- Optional `penetration`, `ricochet`, `heat`, `spreadDegrees`, `projectileLifeSeconds`.
- Agent can add fields but must keep old save data valid and update validators.

## Fire acceptance
1. Mobile with auto-fire ON targets nearest **visible** valid enemy in range and fires automatically.
2. OFF requires explicit input (manual FIRE button).
3. Agent weapon appears clearly next to stationary-pose keeper.
4. Hits decrease HP exactly once each and cannot pass through solid collision blockers.
5. Special triggers only when stated condition occurs.
6. Distinct visible animation states: idle, windup, fire, projectile, impact, special.
7. HUD displays actual runtime damage/cooldown, not stale hard-coded labels.

## Security / practical limits
Build-time agent decides and draws; do not assume Project0 supports live AI generation, network image services, external accounts, or API keys within game runtime. Runtime loot can use seeded procedural variations from approved modular components.

nodes.title: Weapon Families & Loot Evolution
nodes.content:
# Weapon Families and Mutations

## Eight candidate families for later agent creations
1. **Wickpiercer** — harpoon / flare / delayed ignition.
2. **Glasswake** — rotating Fresnel-lens beam reflecting off polished surfaces.
3. **Saltwake Bell** — area ringing attack; increases damage near cursed water.
4. **Mariner's Hook** — ricocheting thrown chain returns to keeper.
5. **Fogmouth** — short cone of salt spray that reveals invisible threats.
6. **Tideglass Needle** — crystalline beam that splits after each ricochet.
7. **Blackwater Lamp** — orbiting oil-fire familiar and corrosive puddles.
8. **The Last Buoy** — delayed explosive marker detonates after a dodge.

## Loot rules
- Starting weapon is unique (one active slot), forged by agent at build time.
- In-run upgrades modify damage, attack rate, projectile count, status effect, reach or special shape.
- Two rare upgrades may change the special function: `Chain Flare` or `Refraction`.
- Post-boss loot can yield a second agent-authored weapon, but enforce weapon asset + JSON + tested mechanics.
- Weapon descriptions and rarity colours should never replace clear numeric differences.

## Naming guidance
Avoid copying recognizable weapon names, images or sound from existing games. Names should suggest brass, sea, light, salt and horror; no franchise references.

nodes.title: Eight Levels Under the Lighthouse
nodes.content:
# Eight Descending Strata

The geography should gradually deform, never cut straight from cozy stone cellar to generic flames. Familiar lighthouse props recur in corrupted forms.

| Depth | Level theme | Normal anchor | Hellish escalation | Main hazard | New enemy | Guardian |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **Lighthouse Top** | keeper's desk, lamp, rain | unsettling vibration | none | none | none |
| 1 | **The Ordinary Cellar** | fuel drums, service stairs | a second door that isn't on plans | falling shelves | Rats | Storage Warden (optional) |
| 2 | **Flooded Maintenance** | pumps, pipes, valves | brackish water flows upward | conductive puddles | Drowned Wisp | The Pumpman |
| 3 | **Salt Chapel** | old coastguard chapel | chapel walls whisper names | salt spikes | Saltbound | Choir of Rust |
| 4 | **Fungus Quarters** | crew bunks, linen closet | beds root into flesh | spore bursts | Husk Bloom | Mother Spore |
| 5 | **Brass Furnace** | generator machinery | cogs grind bones | timed heat vents | Furnace Imp | Furnace Saint |
| 6 | **Drowned Catacombs** | shipwreck stores | drowned corpses in suspended water | tide surges | Anchor Revenant | Drowned Captain |
| 7 | **Abyssal Lens** | beacon lens motifs | light bends and lies | false safe zones | Lens Wraith | False Keeper |
| 8 | **The Buried Sun** | lighthouse beam | fully infernal impossible space | arena light inversion | Sunless Guardian | The Lantern Below |

## Room structure
- 2–4 random rooms per floor; final room of a major floor can be a boss arena.
- Each room has `seed`, `depth`, `biome`, `shape`, `spawnTable`, `hazards`, `reward`, `exits`.
- Encounter budget increases by depth: `budget = 3 + depth*2 + floor(roomIndex/2)` with elite cap.
- A `safeEntryRadius` keeps spawn positions ≥ 135px from keeper.
- Multiple room silhouettes: square, T, cross, broken ring, pump corridor, flooded hall.

## Escalation language
Depth 1: soft rain and low amber light; depth 3: whispers, shadows and wrong windows; depth 5: rust and bone; depth 8: distorted lens flare / impossible sun. Accessibility: motion and flashing must be adjustable.

nodes.title: Enemies and Boss Patterns
nodes.content:
# Enemies and Bosses

## Standard enemy templates
| Enemy | Depth debut | HP | Behaviour |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Bilge Rat | 1 | 20 | rushes keeper, melee contact |
| Drowned Wisp | 2 | 28 | circles keeper, launches visible slow bolts |
| Saltbound | 3 | 46 | windup → dash, leaves salt trail |
| Husk Bloom | 4 | 40 | periodically releases spore warning circles |
| Furnace Imp | 5 | 55 | telegraphed ranged fan attack |
| Anchor Revenant | 6 | 95 | slow advance, frontal cone swing |
| Lens Wraith | 7 | 52 | phantom duplicates, true body carries light |
| Sunless Guardian | 8 | 180 | beam arcs, exposes safe lanes |

## Boss pattern principles
Each major boss has 3–4 attacks, strong telegraphs, cooldown windows, and a recognizable silhouette at low resolution. No 1-frame-hit surprise. Add additional mechanics by floor rather than pure HP inflation.

## Example: The Pumpman (Depth 2)
- Phase 1: magnetic chain pulls water puddles toward center; safe edges visible.
- Phase 2: crossing valves electrify with 0.7s striped warning.
- Vulnerability opens after a 1.2s overpressure animation; player can dodge through an incoming chain, not through walls.

## Example: The False Keeper (Depth 7)
- Uses a mirrored static keeper portrait. Their weapon is the corrupt silhouette of the starter weapon.
- Throws delayed shadow lances that fake your auto-target lock. Telegraph clearly displays true lane vs decoy.

## First playable scope
Bilge Rat, Wisp, Saltbound, Furnace Imp plus one guardian with windup and area attack. Other boss designs are roadmap content, not asserted complete.

nodes.title: Procedural Room Generator
nodes.content:
# Random Room Generation Contract

## Generation algorithm
1. Derive deterministic room seed from run seed + depth + room index.
2. Choose one allowed room silhouette and place 2–6 large collision obstacles avoiding entrance, hatch and a 135px spawn-safe region.
3. Choose props from `normal`, `twisted`, `infernal` palette depending on `depth`.
4. Select weighted hazards by depth; no unavoidable instant damage.
5. Spend encounter budget on enemy pack templates rather than spawning enemies uniformly everywhere.
6. Assign exit hatch; lock until combat ends (or after a specified survival timer).
7. Add reward: embers / chest / shrine / story note / secret.
8. Validate path exists between entrance and exit using flood fill; regenerate failed layouts.

## Room modifiers (chance increases with depth)
- **Flicker:** periodic lantern darkness, telegraphed.
- **Flood:** shallow water slows movement outside raised tiles.
- **Echo:** enemies briefly respawn as weaker spectral copies.
- **Wrong Door:** an extra locked door holds a rare treasure or mimic.
- **Oblique Light:** floor warning lines appear as lens refractions.
- **Reverse Tide:** slow moving hazard sweeps wall to wall.

## Telegraphed hazards
- Water arc: striped warning 0.6s before discharge.
- Vent: glowing floor grate, 0.7s before heat jet.
- Bell: expanding circle 0.65s before impact.
- Avoid random invisible traps; readability first.

## Difficulty & QA
- Seed display in pause for bug reporting.
- Ensure enemies never spawn on top of player / inside solid obstacle.
- Ensure hatches are reachable after every chamber, including touch-only players.
- Keep the first room of Depth 1 easy with optional tutorial labels; deeper layouts gradually gain twists.

## Enemies
- [ ] Rat idle/walk/attack/hurt/death
- [ ] Wisp float/cast/hurt/death
- [ ] Saltbound walk/telegraph/dash/hurt/death

## Boss action set per guardian

## Environment / interactables

## Naming convention
`assets/sprites/<actor>/<actor>_<action>.png` (e.g. `assets/sprites/keeper/keeper_dodge.png`). Every exported animation must be described in `data/sprite-atlas-manifest.json`. **Do not leave frame-layout assumptions in code only.**

nodes.title: Art Direction & Lighting
nodes.content:
# Art Direction

## Visual evolution
**Above ground / depth 1:** lantern amber `#F1C677`, desaturated timber, soot slate `#28313A`, wet greys.
**Depth 2–3:** salt white, algae turquoise `#538C8D`, cold mist.
**Depth 4–5:** red fungal pulp `#9A424F`, furnace copper `#C7602E`, deep shadows.
**Depth 6–7:** drowned violet `#665A90`, cosmic blue `#5261B6`, false gold.
**Depth 8:** charcoal void `#09070C`, blood orange `#E5573F`, reversed white-light beam.

## Lighting
Keep character silhouette bright enough for phone. The lantern creates a dim pool of light; it must not obscure hazards under accessibility contrast mode. Avoid critical information conveyed only by colour. Avoid full-screen strobing and provide reduced-motion toggle.

## UI
Upper left: HP, depth, room, weapon icon. Upper right: settings gear. Lower left: floating joystick. Lower right: dodge cooldown/button; manual fire button appears when Auto Fire is off. Level-up overlay uses 3 large cards, fits portrait and landscape.

## Fidelity and performance
Actual sprites might be produced by an agent later. The standalone prototype intentionally uses clean Canvas primitive shapes and light effects as placeholders. Do not mistake the guide PNGs for finished textured art.

nodes.title: Sprite Atlas Standard
nodes.content:
# Sprite Sheet Layout — Universal Contract

**Assets are sprite sheets, not prose placeholders.** Templates are included in the Asset Library: `player-action-template.png`, `weapon-action-template.png`, `enemy-action-template.png`, `boss-action-template.png`, `vfx-action-template.png`, and the annotated `sprite-atlas-layout.png`. Each includes alignment/safe-zone guides.

## Player and directional enemies
- Separate PNG per **animation action**, e.g. `keeper_idle.png`, `keeper_dodge.png`, `rat_hurt.png`.
- Each action page has **8 columns × 8 rows** with transparent background.
- **64×64 pixel cells** → sheet size **512×512** for player, smaller enemies and handheld weapons.
- Columns = frame index **0…7** (left to right). Rows = direction index **0…7** from top to bottom: `N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW`.
- Frames with no sprite for short actions may remain transparent; `frameCount` in manifest tells runtime how many valid frames to animate. Do NOT sample blank frames.
- Character feet / collision anchor: cell center `x=32,y=52`; weapons use origin `x=32,y=32`.
- No margin or spacing between atlas cells (runtime uses exact `x = frame*64; y = direction*64`).

## Bosses & large effects
- Boss actions: 8×8 grid, **128px cells** → **1024×1024** page.
- Directionless effects/props: **8 columns × 1 row**, 128px cells, **1024×128** PNG. Runtime uses row zero only.
- UI icons: **32×32** one image or atlas icons grid; pixel-perfect nearest-neighbour when upscaled.

## Suggested animation library
| Actor or system | Required actions | Frame counts (initial) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Keeper | idle, walk, dodge, hurt, death, interact | 4, 6, 6, 3, 8, 6 |
| Weapon | idle, windup, fire, reload, special | 4, 3, 4, 6, 8 |
| Projectiles | fly, impact | 4, 6 |
| Bilge Rat | idle, walk, attack, hurt, death | 4, 6, 5, 3, 6 |
| Drowned Wisp | float, cast, hurt, death | 6, 6, 3, 7 |
| Saltbound | walk, telegraph, dash, hurt, death | 6, 4, 4, 3, 8 |
| Furnace Imp | idle, walk, fire, hurt, death | 4, 6, 5, 3, 7 |
| Each boss | idle, move, telegraph, attack, hurt, phase, death | 4, 6, 6, 8, 3, 8, 8 |
| Environment | lamp-flicker, hatch-open, water-ripple, vent-warning, vent-fire, chest-open | 8, 8, 8, 6, 8, 8 |
| VFX | muzzle, hit, flare-detonation, dodge-trail, heal, curse, levelup | 6, 6, 8, 6, 6, 8, 8 |

## Static avatar exception
Only `keeper_idle` frame `[row=4 (S), col=0]` is mandatory for MVP. In static-avatar mode the animator intentionally uses this one cell for moving, firing and dodging; the weapon, glow and afterimages still animate separately. Remaining sheets are optional extensions that must follow the exact same contract once added.

## Metadata keys
`entity`, `action`, `path`, `cellWidth`, `cellHeight`, `columns`, `rows`, `directions`, `frameCount`, `fps`, `loop`, `pivot`, `renderScale`, `events`.

## Test vectors
- Frame 3 facing west (`directionIndex = 6`) of 64px atlas → source rect `(192,384,64,64)`.
- Frame 7 facing south-east (`index=3`) of 128px boss atlas → source rect `(896,384,128,128)`.
- All atlas images must be RGBA transparent, with no embedded cell guide labels in final game artwork.

nodes.title: Master Agent Build Prompt
nodes.content:
# Copy-Paste Project0 Agent Master Brief

You are the lead game designer, artist, programmer, QA and technical integrator for **RELICFALL: Beneath the Beacon**.

## Required first actions
1. Read the attached docs and their canonical names: Game Design Bible; Mobile Settings & Auto Fire; Dodge & Invulnerability; Eight Levels Under the Lighthouse; Agent Weapon Forge Brief; Sprite Atlas Standard; Weapon Data Schema.
2. Read and confirm current authoritative Project0 documentation: `https://project0.city/skill.md`, `https://project0.city/guides/games.md`, `https://project0.city/guides/assets.md`. If they cannot be fetched, log the unknowns instead of guessing or publishing.
3. Independently **create a starter weapon**, inspired by lighthouse parts. Design original sprite / SVG art and projectile VFX, JSON data, functional hit collision, special effect, and animations. Player should never need to create the starting weapon for you.
4. Build a **top-down** mobile-first roguelike. Main character is a **Lighthouse Keeper** with static fallback sprite: moving the still image around counts as valid animation-free avatar movement. All weapon FX, dodges, enemies and environment animate independently.

## Gameplay contract
- On mobile, Auto Fire is **ON on first load**. Settings must permit **ON/OFF** and save choice between visits.
- When OFF, an accessible visible FIRE button must work; when ON, attack nearest eligible visible enemy automatically without penetrating walls.
- Dodge via large phone button and Shift on desktop: 120px / 0.22s, 0.16s i-frames, 1.5s cooldown. Collision against solids required; good afterimage FX.
- Multiple levels descending **beneath the lighthouse**: start with ordinary cellar and gradually become hellish. Distinct depth-specific colours, props, enemies and hazards. Procedurally arrange each room from a seeded RNG, validate reachable exit.
- Add XP, leveling choices, enemy telegraphs, death/restart, room transitions, readable touch HUD.
- Use sprite atlases: 8 columns × 8 direction rows, 64px cells for player/enemies/weapons, 128px for bosses; 8×1 for directionless FX. Obey row ordering `N NE E SE S SW W NW`. Each action has separate file + manifest. MVP can use static keeper S-facing frame 0; do not fake a completed sprite atlas.

## Agent-made weapon section
Always generate actual artwork and structured weapon data, then document tests and balancing. Required `weapons/starter-weapon.json`, `weapons/weapon.schema.json`, sprite or SVG, projectile hit effect and implemented firing logic. Future weapon families from design docs are references, not mandatory for v1.

## Order of implementation
A. Weapon concept, art & working data/attack.
B. Start room, player movement, settings, auto/manual fire, dodge and one enemy.
C. Seeded rooms, depth escalation, telegraphed threats and room hatch transitions.
D. XP/upgrades, enemy variety, one boss and UI polish.
E. Test on mobile & desktop, log verified vs unverified, produce platform integration package.

## Important safety and launch limits
Do not assume Project0 exposes custom avatar models or permits arbitrary remote assets. Do not paste keys into JS. Do not claim a multiplayer/saving feature is tested until verified. Do not publish the live lot or irreversibly replace existing work without explicit owner approval. Prioritize a functional playable prototype over oversized promises.

## Deliverables
1. Full source; 2. artwork files (not merely prompts); 3. data schema/manifest; 4. a running prototype; 5. test log with device context; 6. precise Project0 integration steps and limitations; 7. list of incomplete features.

nodes.title: Project0 Integration Unknowns
nodes.content:
# Project0 Integration — verification required

The design package and playable prototype are general browser artifacts, NOT automatically a published Project0 experience. Before binding to a lot, read these living documents directly:
- `https://project0.city/skill.md`
- `https://project0.city/guides/games.md`
- `https://project0.city/guides/assets.md`

## Unknowns to verify
- Accepted game source file format, code size, permitted dependencies / external URLs.
- Whether game runs in iframe, isolated JS, canvas, sandbox with restricted input/audio.
- Lifecycle hooks, save-state/score APIs, click/touch behaviour on mobile.
- Ability to access actual user avatar assets from inside a game.
- Entry, exit, and multiplayer assumptions; moderation/licensing requirements.
- Lot ownership and publication rights.

## Safe fallback
Host the game as self-contained Canvas app first. Keep a static portrait fallback for character. Do not code around unverified internal endpoints, scrape live player/account data, or embed API keys. Do not overwrite an existing public lot without explicit approval.

nodes.title: QA Checklist & Acceptance Tests
nodes.content:
# QA & Acceptance Tests

## Core
- [ ] Actual Lighthouse Keeper renders and moves with static fallback sprite.
- [ ] Camera and UI retain readable 2D layout in both 390×844 and desktop.
- [ ] All visible enemies in range can be attacked; walls block projectiles.
- [ ] On fresh mobile storage, auto-fire is ON and fires within weapon cooldown.
- [ ] Toggle OFF → immediately stops auto-fire and shows manual FIRE button.
- [ ] Toggle ON → restores attack; preference survives reload.
- [ ] Two-finger input: joystick + dodge do not steal each other's touch.
- [ ] Dodge distance/duration approximately match config, walls block it.
- [ ] Damage during 0.16-s iframe does nothing; damage afterward applies.
- [ ] Dodge cooldown shown accurately and no hold-to-spam.

## Procedural world
- [ ] Room RNG reproducible by run seed + depth + room index.
- [ ] Each room provides a safe spawn gap and reachable exit.
- [ ] Depth 1 looks like regular maintenance cellar.
- [ ] Themes visibly degrade over at least 8 distinct depth stages.
- [ ] Enemy attack warnings are visible without colour perception.
- [ ] Death and restart restore appropriate stats.

## Art/data
- [ ] Every animation page has matching manifest frame count and dimensions.
- [ ] 64px directional sheet is 512×512, boss sheet 1024×1024, VFX sheet 1024×128.
- [ ] Sprite cell coordinates test correctly (e.g. W frame3 = 192,384,64,64).
- [ ] Weapon art is generated by agent and actually included, not a text-only claim.
- [ ] Starting weapon file passes schema validation, including special proc.

## Project0
- [ ] Documentation fetched and exact host APIs confirmed.
- [ ] Mobile iframe/sandbox/pointer events tested on site.
- [ ] File/asset size and remote dependency rules verified.
- [ ] No API keys appear in shipped files.
- [ ] Public publication authorized by user.

**Report pass/fail with actual evidence rather than tick everything preemptively.**

nodes.title: Artwork References & Asset Requests
nodes.content:
# Reference & Asset Requests

## Avatar request
Produce a 64x64 transparent 2D Lighthouse Keeper idle sprite, front view south; weatherworn yellow oilskin coat, lantern in left hand, sea boots, brass keys. Keep strong silhouette, dark fantasy pixel-art style, readable at 32px. No platform franchise imagery.

## Weapon agent request
See **Agent Weapon Forge Brief** and **Agent Asset Request Template**. The starter weapon must be invented by the agent, not designed from a downloaded existing franchise texture.

## Environment requests
- Level 1 dry timber floor / intact brass valve / normal fuel barrel.
- Level 2 flooded pipe / broken pump / foam and bubbles.
- Level 3 salt-glass chapel window / still prayer bench.
- Level 4 rooted bunk bed / fungal spore pods.
- Level 5 infernal furnace vent / brass gear.
- Level 6 drowned bones / drifting seaweed.
- Level 7 bending Fresnel glass / double shadows.
- Level 8 inverted beacon and black sun.

## File rules
PNG RGBA with transparent background for characters/VFX; nearest-neighbour for pixel art. Follow atlas contract. Keep layers separate and embed metadata in JSON. Only upload assets you own or have permission to use.
